text:
Alex Kim: anyone else seeing a p99/502 spike from hosted-infer gateway starting ~08:12 UTC? Support ticket #4532 has multiple customers reporting timeouts + 502s when calling /v1/generate. Gateway SLO alert just fired. Unsure if this is authz, upstream model pods, or proxy backlog.

sre-bot: [ALERT] hosted-infer.gateway.request_latency_p99 > 1200ms (10m). Alert id: alert-7832. Affected regions: us-west-2, eu-west-1.

Tara Singh: oncall here. Looking at console — p95 OK, p99 is the issue. Spike concentrated on short requests (<=512 tokens). No deploys in last 2 hours. Dashboards show increased upstream 502/504 and a small bump in `envoy.upstream_rq_pending_overflow`.

Mike O'Connor: grabbing traces. Sampling shows a chunk of requests with missing model-proxy spans -> trace gap. Checking logs now. Query I'm running (Datadog logs):

```
service:gateway status:[500 TO 599] @path:/v1/generate | group_by(status, model_variant) | limit 20
```

Mike O'Connor: results: surge of 502 from model-proxy with reason `upstream_reset` and `connection failure`. Also seeing `TLS handshake timeout` at the proxy side for a subset. Looks like some upstream pods rejecting or TCP resets.

Irene Zhao: CS update: customer A observed ~30% failure rate for ~5-10 minutes, retried and succeeded. Customer B reports retried 5 times and gave up. They asked if billing tokens were charged for failed attempts — we should loop billing.

Tara Singh: can someone check model-proxy pool metrics? specifically `open_connections`, `pending_requests`, `worker_loop_latency` and `max_conns` consumption. If pool exhaustion -> envoys will reset. Also check whether KV-cache lookups are stalling (we've seen that produce head-of-line blocks).

Mike O'Connor: running quick k8s exec into model-proxy pod in us-west-2: `kubectl -n hosted-infer exec -it proxy-65f9 -- /bin/sh` and tailing logs. I see repeated: `ERROR upstream reset: reason=Connection reset by peer (errno=104)`. Also a handful of `authz: token validation timeout` logs (which map to upstream authz service at 10.4.2.12).

Alex Kim: interesting — two signals: authz timeouts and upstream connection resets. Could be authz causing delayed acceptance, then client times out and proxy resets. Tara, can we correlate authz latency with these requests?

Tara Singh: running a short query against tracing index to correlate spans. Query: `service:gateway -> service:authz` latencies. Preliminary: authz p99 jumped from 30ms to ~900ms at same time window. Looks like authz sidecar had GC pause / DB call delay.

Mike O'Connor: also spotted H2 window stalls in the proxy logs, a few `RST_STREAM` from model backends after ~10s. That plus authz delay == cascading timeouts.

Alex Kim: quick mitigation: can we flip gateway fallback-policy to skip authz for internal-trusted routes (only for a short window) and route to warm model pool? Alternatively increase envoy upstream timeout from 15s -> 30s while we triage. Pros/cons?

Tara Singh: I don't want to disable authz globally. Short-term we can: 1) increase upstream timeout to 30s for model-proxy in us-west-2 via feature-flag (safe rollback), 2) enable route-level `circuit_breaker` to allow more concurrent conns to healthy pods. I'll open a small config canary.

Mike O'Connor: I pushed a canary config to the model-proxy config-map (us-west-2) increasing `upstream_timeout_ms: 30000` and bumping `max_connections` for the worker from 100 -> 200. Deployed to 2 pods. Deploy job id: deploy-9921.

sre-bot: deploy job deploy-9921 started. CI checks passed.

Tara Singh: monitoring. So far error rate down from 28% -> 6% in the canary region. p99 latency still elevated but trending down.

Irene Zhao: passing update to customers: half reported immediate improvement; one still seeing intermittent errors and wants credit if billed for failed calls. I'll open billing query and save logs for chargeback.

Alex Kim: good. Mike, can you open an issue for authz latency root cause and tag infra/authz team? We need spans and heap/GC metrics for the authz service. Also capture model-proxy tcpdump snippet if possible.

Mike O'Connor: will do. Created ticket INFRA-1209 with initial logs, trace ids, and tcpdump sample (attached). Also flagged the authz team: @authz-service.

Tara Singh: postmortem items:
- follow up authz perf investigation (INFRA-1209)
- consider local authz cache for short TTL to reduce p99 impact
- add more aggressive health checks for model-backends to avoid RST_STREAM cascades
- add observability alert for `authz.p99 > 100ms` tied to gateway SLO to reduce firefighting time

Alex Kim: +1. Also add a quick runbook note: if authz p99 spike detected, canary increasing upstream timeout + bumping max_conns has been effective as temporary mitigation.

sre-bot: [RESOLVED] alert-7832. Incident window: 08:12 - 08:45 UTC.

Irene Zhao: customers updated; one support escalation converted to credit request. I'm logging follow-up with billing.

Tara Singh: closing oncall for this. Will keep INFRA-1209 in triage for next-week RCA. If anyone sees regression ping here or escalate to incidents. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Alex Kim: thanks team. Leaving thread open for any lingering traces.
